saints.name: St. Turibius of Mogrovejo
saints.title: Archbishop of Lima
saints.shortBlurb: The Spanish lawyer who became archbishop of Lima and a tireless reformer and evangelizer of colonial Peru…
biography: Born in 1538 at Mayorga in León, Turibius taught law at Salamanca and was serving as a lay judge of the Inquisition at Granada when Philip II named him, over his own protest, to the see of Lima. Ordained priest in 1578 and consecrated in 1580, he reached Peru in 1581.

Three times he traversed his vast archdiocese on foot, baptizing and confirming — among them St. Rose of Lima and St. Martín de Porres — learning the native tongues, and defending the Indians against the abuses of the colonists. He presided over the Third Council of Lima in 1582–83 and in 1591 founded the first seminary in the Americas.

Worn by fever on a visitation, he died at Zaña on 23 March 1606, repeating the Lord's own words, "into thy hands I commend my spirit." Canonized by Benedict XIII in 1726, he was proclaimed patron of the Latin American episcopate by John Paul II in 1983.
saints.knownFor: The evangelization and reform of the Church in Peru.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 23 March
